42867538.label: Objectives
42867538.text: To develop and validate a preoperative gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI-based radiomics model for predicting the time to advanced-stage recurrence in patients undergoing resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

42867538.label: Materials and methods
42867538.text: This retrospective single-center study included patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage 0/A HCC who underwent resection between 2009 and 2014. Patients were temporally divided into training (n = 272; 2009-2011) and validation (n = 210; 2012-2014) cohorts. Time to advanced-stage recurrence was defined as the interval from resection to macrovascular invasion and/or extrahepatic metastasis. Two radiologists segmented tumors on hepatobiliary phase images, followed by 3-mm peritumoral expansion and propagation to co-registered dynamic T1- and T2-weighted images. After extraction of Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative-compliant features, a radiomics model was developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression. Model performance and inter-reader reproducibility of binary risk stratification were evaluated using the concordance index (C-index) and Cohen's kappa, respectively.

42867538.label: Results
42867538.text: Five-year advanced-stage recurrence occurred in 15% of the training (42/272) and validation (32/210) cohorts. In the validation cohort, the radiomics model yielded a C-index of 0.716 (95% CI, 0.631-0.801). This outperformed the preoperative BCLC (0.597; 95% CI 0.551-0.644) and Hong Kong Liver Cancer (0.594; 95% CI 0.516-0.672) staging systems, and was equivalent to the postoperative clinicopathological model (0.716; 95% CI 0.626-0.807). Radiomic-based risk stratification showed good inter-reader reproducibility (kappa = 0.757).

42867538.label: Conclusion
42867538.text: The preoperative radiomics model outperformed staging systems and was comparable to the postoperative clinicopathological model in predicting advanced-stage recurrence, relying entirely on noninvasive data.

42870138.label: Objective
42870138.text: MRI is increasingly used to assess treatment response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but only qualitatively. This study evaluates the reproducibility and predictive value of quantitative apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), thought to be a non-invasive surrogate for tumor cell density, in patients with MIBC receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy.

42870138.label: Materials and methods
42870138.text: MRI data from 35 patients, enrolled in the Phase-Ib NABUCCO trial, were analyzed. ADC maps were derived from pre- and post-treatment MRI scans. Three independent radiologists assessed multiple regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate inter-observer agreement and predictive performance for pathological complete response (pCR). ADC values were normalized using muscle tissue as a reference. Additionally, we analyzed the correlation between ADC and cell densities, derived from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) data.

42870138.label: Results
42870138.text: ADC measurements from the whole-tumor ROI (n = 25) demonstrated the highest reproducibility (0.98, 95% CI = [0.95-0.99]), but lacked predictive value (AUC = 0.31, 95% CI = [0.12-0.53], p = 0.109). The most hypointense ROI (n = 22) showed the strongest predictive value for pCR (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.57-1], p = 0.025), though with limited reproducibility. The difference between baseline and follow-up ADC values in the hypointense region (n = 20) again showed the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.58-0.98], p = 0.015). Although muscle normalization is proposed to reduce scanner variability, it did not improve predictive performance in this cohort and occasionally reduced reproducibility. No significant correlation was found between whole-tumor ADC and cell density.

42870138.label: Conclusion
42870138.text: Despite analyzing different measurement techniques for ADC values, none was simultaneously reproducible and predictive, nor provided insights into the biology of the tumor. While ADC shows promise in MIBC, there is an urgent need for more standardized, robust imaging biomarkers.

42870138.label: Key points
42870138.text: Question Non-invasive biomarkers are urgently needed to guide bladder-preserving strategies in MIBC. Findings DWI-MRI shows promise, but standardized robust imaging biomarkers are essential for reliable response assessment. Critical relevance statement Standardized or AI-assisted ROI segmentation could improve ADC reproducibility and diagnostic accuracy in multicenter studies.

42899938.text: Background Maintaining diagnostic CT image quality in patients with obesity remains challenging because increased x-ray attenuation is often offset by higher radiation exposure. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) has demonstrated improved dose efficiency and image quality, but intraindividual data in this population are limited. Purpose To compare radiation dose, quantitative image quality, and subjective image quality between PCCT and energy-integrating detector (EID) CT intraindividually in patients with obesity. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with obesity undergoing thoracic and/or abdominal CT at both PCCT and EID CT between December 1, 2022, and January 31, 2025. Signal, image noise, and signal to noise ratio (SNR) were measured in vascular, parenchymal, muscular, and adipose tissue. Two radiologists independently rated image quality on a six-point Likert scale. Radiation dose parameters were volume CT dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and effective dose. The paired two-sided t test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for group comparisons. Results This study included 51 patients with obesity (median age, 56 years [IQR, 51-66.5 years]; 33 male). Signal was higher with PCCT than EID CT in vascular structures, parenchymal organs, and muscle and more negative in subcutaneous fat (all P < .001), with similar image noise (P = .09-.84). SNR was higher with PCCT in vascular structures (ascending aorta: mean, 19.65 ± 6.47 [SD] vs 13.22 ± 4.83; P < .001) and most parenchymal organs (liver: 5.53 ± 1.69 vs 4.71 ± 1.89; P = .02). The difference in SNR increased with body mass index for vessels (r = 0.36) and parenchymal organs (r = 0.51) (both P < .001). Both readers rated overall image quality, contrast, and sharpness higher and artifact-related impairment lower for PCCT (all P < .001), whereas subjective image noise was similar (P = .16 and .14). CTDIvol (median, 11.99 vs 17.05 mGy) and DLP (median, 526.25 vs 709.32 mGy · cm) were lower with PCCT (both P < .001). Conclusion In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT.

42937538.text: Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (P for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2300075711

42955038.text: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the United States, and accurate pretreatment evaluation is essential for risk stratification, treatment planning, and detection of recurrent disease. This evidence-based review summarizes imaging recommendations for patients with established endometrial cancer undergoing pretreatment assessment, surveillance, or evaluation for suspected recurrence. MRI pelvis without and with intravenous contrast is usually appropriate for assessment of local tumor extension across histologic subtypes and grades. For aggressive histologic tumor types, or when metastatic disease is suspected, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for evaluation of nodal and distant metastases. Routine imaging surveillance is usually not appropriate for asymptomatic patients with treated low- or intermediate-risk disease, whereas CT may be appropriate in selected asymptomatic high-risk patients. MRI pelvis, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for suspected recurrence. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision process support the systematic analysis of the medical literature from peer reviewed journals. Established methodology principles such as Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE are adapted to evaluate the evidence. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method User Manual provides the methodology to determine the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where peer reviewed literature is lacking or equivocal, experts may be the primary evidentiary source available to formulate a recommendation.

42957938.label: Objectives
42957938.text: To develop a non-invasive diagnostic model combining magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived proton density fat fraction (PDFF) and adipose tissue for identifying metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

42957938.label: Materials and methods
42957938.text: A total of 197 consecutive patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) who underwent liver biopsy, MRI-PDFF, and transient elastography (TE) were retrospectively enrolled. Independent predictors of MASH were identified using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A combined model was constructed and internally validated via 1000 bootstrap resamples. The diagnostic performance was compared with that of established non-invasive tests (NITs).

42957938.label: Results
42957938.text: Multivariable logistic regression analyses demonstrated that the PDFF and total adipose tissue index (TATI) were independent risk factors for MASH. The MRI-based PDFF-adipose tissue (MR-PAT) model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.866 for MASH identification. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an AUC of 0.870. The performance of the models was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. The diagnostic performance of the MR-PAT model for MASH identification was significantly better than that of all the established NITs (all p < 0.05).

42957938.label: Conclusion
42957938.text: The MR-PAT model, combining MRI-derived PDFF and TATI, provides an accurate and robust non-invasive tool for identifying MASH. It outperforms widely recognized NITs and holds promise for risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

42957938.label: Key points
42957938.text: Question MASH is a critical histological endpoint of MASLD, but reliable non-invasive tools for its assessment remain inadequate. Findings The MR-PAT model integrating MRI-based PDFF and adipose tissue quantification demonstrates robust and excellent diagnostic performance for identifying MASH. Critical Relevance Statement The MR-PAT model leverages hepatic steatosis and the adipose tissue burden to elucidate the pathophysiological mechanisms driving steatohepatitis. It can serve as an accurate, non-invasive tool for identifying MASH and holds promise for risk stratification in patients with MASLD.

42971888.label: Background
42971888.text: Current stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF) relies on clinical factors with known limitations. Blood stasis in the Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) promotes thrombus formation, contributing to embolic stroke. Our objective is to map contrast transport throughout the LAA volume with 4DCT.

42971888.label: Methods
42971888.text: Patients being treated for AF underwent dynamic contrast 4DCT. Hounsfield unit (HU) vs. time curves were fitted voxel wise using gamma-variate models. Three LAA blood transport metrics were extracted: (1) increase in residence time between distal LAA voxels and the LA/LAA orifice (ΔRT); (2) ratio of peak HU enhancement in distal LAA voxels to peak HU in the LA/LAA orifice (ΔHU); and (3) total volume of delayed filling (Vstasis) in the LAA. A composite "LAA Transport Index" (LAATI) was computed using principal component analysis.

42971888.label: Results
42971888.text: Among all 93 patients, a wide range of delayed transport in the LAA was observed with: 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​30 ​s, 0.02 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​13 ​mL. Patients imaged during sinus rhythm (n ​= ​26) had rapid filling of the entire LAA with 0 ​< ​ΔRT ​< ​4.7 ​s, 0.65 ​< ​ΔHU ​< ​1, 0 ​< ​Vstasis ​< ​1.0 ​mL. In comparison, patients in AF had values over the entire range ΔRT, ΔHU and Vstasis. For patients imaged in sinus the mean LAATI ​= ​-1.06 ​± ​0.4, and for those imaged in AF the mean LAATI ​= ​0.43 ​± ​1.7. LAATI did not correlate with CHA2DS2-VASc (p ​= ​0.44) or chicken wing morphology (p ​= ​0.21).

42971888.label: Conclusions
42971888.text: 4DCT-based voxel-wise quantification of LAA contrast transport using gamma-variate modeling is technically feasible. Further studies are required to determine its potential value for personalized stroke-risk assessment.

43004088.label: Objectives
43004088.text: This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning model that integrates T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for the noninvasive prediction of muscle invasion in bladder cancer.

43004088.label: Materials and methods
43004088.text: A total of 308 bladder tumors from 254 patients were retrospectively collected from three institutions. Of these, 177 tumors from Center 1 were partitioned via stratified sampling into a training set (n = 128) and an internal validation set (n = 49). The remaining two centers contributed 59 and 72 tumors, respectively, which served as external validation cohorts. A dual-branch 3D deep convolutional neural network (Joint model) based on biparametric MRI (bp-MRI) was developed using the training data and compared with a deep learning model based on T2WI (T2WI model) and VI-RADS assessments by radiologists. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.

43004088.label: Results
43004088.text: The Joint model achieved mean AUCs of 0.979 ± 0.007 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.907 ± 0.013 and 0.916 ± 0.021 in the external validation cohorts. It outperformed the T2WI model in all cohorts and achieved higher AUCs than radiologists across all validation cohorts. Notably, for equivocal VI-RADS 2-3 lesions, the Joint model yielded higher accuracy than the T2WI model in external validation.

43004088.label: Conclusion
43004088.text: Compared with the T2WI model and VI-RADS assessment, the Joint model demonstrated better diagnostic performance and generalizability for predicting muscle invasion in patients with bladder cancer.

43004088.label: Key points
43004088.text: Question Reliable noninvasive tools for preoperative prediction of muscle invasion in bladder cancer are lacking, as TURBT-based staging carries procedural risks and frequent understaging. Findings A biparametric MRI deep learning model achieved AUCs of 0.907-0.979 across internal and external validation cohorts, outperforming T2WI-only models and VI-RADS. Critical relevance statement Contrast-free biparametric MRI combined with deep learning enables accurate, generalizable preoperative prediction of muscle invasion, offering particular value for equivocal VI-RADS 2-3 lesions and supporting noninvasive clinical decision-making.

43019238.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen-targeted PET agents are mainly used for prostate cancer; however, uptake in non-prostatic inflammatory tissue can challenge the physician. We report the case of a 75-year-old man referred for characterization of an FDG-avid prostate focus with normal PSA. 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT was performed. Incidental moderate symmetric uptake was found in the pelvic-girdle and paravertebral muscles, without morphologic correlate on CT. Elevated creatine kinase, a late scleroderma-pattern capillaroscopy, and muscle MRI confirmed scleroderma-associated myositis. This case emphasizes that symmetric muscular prostate-specific membrane antigen uptake can reveal active inflammatory myositis.

43023938.text: A 50-year-old woman presented to our hospital with lower abdominal pain for 1 week. Pelvic CT revealed a significantly enlarged uterus with multiple nodular and mass lesions. Subsequently, the patient underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT examination.18F-FDG PET/CT revealed multiple nodules and mass lesions in the uterus with intense 18F-FDG uptake. The patient underwent needle biopsy of the uterine lesion. Histopathologic and immunohistochemical findings revealed uterine adenomyoma. This case suggests that uterine adenomyoma with intense FDG uptake is easily misdiagnosed as malignancy, and diagnosis should be confirmed by pathology.

43026438.label: Background
43026438.text: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cell therapies for solid tumours face challenges regarding inefficient trafficking to the tumour site, limited extravasation and impaired persistence within an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Non-invasive imaging approaches capable of capturing the dynamic behaviour and biodistribution of CAR T cells are therefore needed to better understand these barriers. This study explores the use of compartmental modelling to interpret technetium-99 m pertechnetate ([99mTc]TcO4-) uptake by CAR T cells co-expressing the sodium iodide symporter (NIS) reporter gene in a prostate cancer NSG mouse model using single-photon emission computed tomography computerised tomography (SPECT/CT).

43026438.label: Results
43026438.text: Co-expression of hNIS with a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) targeting CAR did not impair CAR T cell function and enabled non-invasive visualisation of CAR-hNIS T cell infiltration in vivo. Dynamic SPECT/CT imaging revealed clear differences in tumour uptake between CAR-hNIS treated mice and control groups. Compartmental modelling using a reversible two-compartment framework demonstrated increased tracer influx and reduced tracer efflux in CAR-hNIS treated tumours. These kinetic changes indicate that tumour signal arises from NIS-mediated tracer uptake and delayed tracer washout in tumours containing infiltrating CAR T cells, rather than from passive perfusion or non-specific delivery alone. Immunohistochemistry confirmed CAR T cell infiltration in the tumours.

43026438.label: Conclusions
43026438.text: This work establishes a proof-of-concept for applying kinetic modelling to interpret CAR T cell infiltration in vivo using dynamic hNIS-based SPECT imaging. By distinguishing tracer delivery from tracer washout kinetics and correcting for variability in tracer bioavailability, this approach provides a more sophisticated biological interpretation of tumour uptake than static imaging alone. These findings highlight the potential of integrating kinetic modelling into future quantitative cell-tracking strategies to improve the evaluation and optimisation of CAR T cell therapies for solid tumours.

43034938.label: Objectives
43034938.text: Overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE) limits the use of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) in portal hypertension. We aimed to determine whether automated three-dimensional (3D) body composition analysis could improve pre-TIPS prediction of overt HE compared with conventional two-dimensional (2D) manual assessment.

43034938.label: Materials and methods
43034938.text: This multicenter study included 593 eligible patients from seven institutions (training cohort: n = 308; external validation 1 cohort: n = 151; and external validation 2 cohort: n = 134). After evaluating L3-based 2D measurements, we developed a fully automated 3D muscle and adipose assessment incorporating morphologic and radiomic features. We combined the 3D assessment with selected clinical variables to predict post-TIPS overt HE risk, and benchmarked the final model against published clinical scores. Model performance was evaluated via ROC analysis, DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and subgroup analyses.

43034938.label: Results
43034938.text: Traditional 2D measurements showed poor reproducibility, with significant variation in 96.2% (25/26) of features. The 3D Model significantly outperformed the 2D Model. The Integrated Model yielded AUCs of 0.78, 0.73, and 0.77 in the training and two external validation cohorts, exceeding those of Child-Pugh, MELD, ALBI, AMMON-OHE, and Lambda (AUCs 0.47-0.64; all p < 0.05). No significant subgroup differences were observed. High-risk patients had 2- to 4-fold higher overt HE incidence. The model reclassified 40.2% of patients with low pre-TIPS ammonia as high risk and 60.2% of those with high ammonia as low risk.

43034938.label: Conclusion
43034938.text: Automated 3D muscle and adipose analysis enables objective preprocedural prediction of overt HE after TIPS, which may facilitate clinical decision-making and optimize patient selection.

43034938.label: Key points
43034938.text: Question Can automated three-dimensional muscle and adipose analysis improve reproducible preprocedural prediction of overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt beyond conventional two-dimensional assessment? Findings In 593 patients from seven hospitals, an Integrated Model combining automated three-dimensional body composition and clinical variables outperformed five published clinical comparator scores. Clinical relevance This fully automated three-dimensional body composition (muscle and adipose) analysis enables objective preprocedural risk stratification for overt hepatic encephalopathy after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, supporting more consistent patient selection.

43070988.label: Purpose
43070988.text: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) shows a longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET signature: acute hypermetabolism in limbic-striatal-thalamic regions and hypometabolism in posterior associative cortex, both partially reversible under immunotherapy. Whether these patterns show spatial correspondence with specific neuromodulatory systems is unknown.

43070988.label: Methods
43070988.text: This retrospective secondary analysis included twenty-two AE patients from a previously published longitudinal cohort (Cerne et al. 2025) who underwent [¹⁸F]FDG PET at clinical baseline (BS) and follow-up (FU). Using JuSpace (option 6), atlas-regional BS-FU difference maps were correlated (Spearman) with 15 normative PET/SPECT maps of multiple neurotransmitter systems. Participant-level Spearman coefficients were Fisher-z transformed. Group inference used paired BS/FU label permutations, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all 15 maps. Spatial co-localization was interpreted as overlap in regional involvement, not as directionality of transmitter signaling. Age-adjusted regression models tested associations between individual JuSpace coefficients and clinical outcomes at BS and FU.

43070988.label: Results
43070988.text: Longitudinal metabolic change showed positive spatial associations with VAChT (Fisher z = 0.164; ρ = 0.185; q = 0.023) and α4β2 (z = 0.133; ρ = 0.127; q = 0.004), and a negative association with 5-HT2A (z = - 0.108; ρ=-0.093; q = 0.014). The cholinergic alignment matches the previously described hypermetabolic limbic-striatal circuit, whereas the 5-HT2A alignment situates reversible posterior hypometabolism within serotonin-enriched association cortex. No exploratory clinical association survived multiplicity correction.

43070988.label: Conclusion
43070988.text: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET differences showed significant spatial correspondence with distinct neuromodulatory territories. Embedding longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes into a normative receptor space provides a systems-level neurochemical framework and generates testable hypotheses on how cholinergic subcortico-limbic and 5-HT2A-enriched posterior association territories relate to acute disease expression and recovery.

43071588.text: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS) rarely presents as an F-18 FDG-avid mass lesion. A 44-year-old man presented with acute slurred speech and right hemiparesis. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a left fronto-temporo-insular mass. F-18 FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography showed intense uptake (SUVmax 12.7; lesion-to-contralateral mirror-ROI ratio 3.3; lesion-to-cortex ratio 1.2), suggesting high-grade glioma, whereas whole-body imaging excluded systemic disease. Resection histopathology identified the mass as PACNS, lymphocytic type, and the patient recovered completely after immunosuppressive therapy. Notably, reported F-18 FDG findings in PACNS are inconsistent; intense avidity does not exclude the diagnosis, and histopathologic confirmation is essential before oncologic treatment.
